question_en: What is the current Long Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax rate on listed equity shares and equity-oriented mutual funds in India, and what is the exemption limit?
question_hi: भारत में सूचीबद्ध इक्विटी शेयरों और इक्विटी-उन्मुख म्यूचुअल फंडों पर वर्तमान दीर्घकालिक पूंजीगत लाभ (LTCG) कर की दर क्या है, और छूट की सीमा क्या है?
question_hinglish: India mein listed equity shares aur equity-oriented mutual funds par current LTCG tax rate kya hai, aur exemption limit kitni hai?
answer: As per Union Budget 2024-25 (effective 23 July 2024), the LTCG tax rate on listed equity shares and equity-oriented mutual funds is 12.5% (previously 10%). The exemption limit has been increased from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 1.25 lakh per financial year. LTCG applies to gains on sale of equity held for more than 12 months.
source: Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Section 112A of Income Tax Act as amended; Union Budget 2024-25 presented on 23 July 2024
explanation: Prior to Budget 2024, LTCG on listed equity was taxed at 10% above Rs 1 lakh exemption (introduced in Budget 2018). The Finance (No. 2) Act 2024 changed this to 12.5% with a Rs 1.25 lakh exemption, effective from 23 July 2024. While the exemption went up by Rs 25,000, the rate increase of 2.5 percentage points means higher tax for most investors with significant gains.

Stating the old 10% rate which was valid from 2018 to July 2024
Stating Rs 1 lakh exemption instead of Rs 1.25 lakh

question_en: What is the Short Term Capital Gains (STCG) tax rate on equity shares and equity-oriented mutual funds sold through a recognized stock exchange in India?
question_hi: भारत में मान्यता प्राप्त स्टॉक एक्सचेंज के माध्यम से बेचे गए इक्विटी शेयरों और इक्विटी-उन्मुख म्यूचुअल फंडों पर अल्पकालिक पूंजीगत लाभ (STCG) कर की दर क्या है?
question_hinglish: India mein recognized stock exchange ke through bechhe gaye equity shares aur equity mutual funds par STCG tax rate kya hai?
answer: As per Union Budget 2024-25 (effective 23 July 2024), Short Term Capital Gains on equity shares and equity-oriented mutual funds (under Section 111A) is taxed at 20%. This applies to shares/units held for 12 months or less and sold on a recognized stock exchange with STT paid.
source: Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Section 111A of Income Tax Act as amended; Union Budget 2024-25 presented on 23 July 2024
explanation: Before Budget 2024, STCG on listed equity under Section 111A was taxed at a flat rate of 15%. This rate had been in place since 2004 when STT was introduced. The Budget 2024 increased this to 20%, a significant 5 percentage point hike, effective 23 July 2024. This was one of the most impactful changes for active traders.

Stating the old 15% rate which was valid from 2004 to July 2024

question_en: What is the standard deduction available to salaried individuals under the new income tax regime in India?
question_hi: भारत में नई आयकर व्यवस्था के तहत वेतनभोगी व्यक्तियों को कितनी मानक कटौती उपलब्ध है?
question_hinglish: India mein new income tax regime ke under salaried individuals ko kitni standard deduction milti hai?
answer: Under the new income tax regime (default regime under Section 115BAC), salaried individuals are entitled to a standard deduction of Rs 75,000 per financial year, effective from FY 2024-25. This was increased from Rs 50,000 in the Union Budget 2024-25.
source: Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Section 115BAC of Income Tax Act as amended; Union Budget 2024-25 dated 23 July 2024
explanation: The standard deduction under the new tax regime was Rs 50,000 (introduced in Budget 2023 when the new regime was revamped and made the default). Budget 2024 increased it to Rs 75,000 specifically for the new regime, effective FY 2024-25. Note: the standard deduction under the old regime remains Rs 50,000. The family pension deduction was also increased from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 under the new regime.

question_en: What is the current Securities Transaction Tax (STT) rate on the sale of options contracts on recognized stock exchanges in India?
question_hi: भारत में मान्यता प्राप्त स्टॉक एक्सचेंजों पर ऑप्शन कॉन्ट्रैक्ट्स की बिक्री पर वर्तमान प्रतिभूति लेनदेन कर (STT) दर क्या है?
question_hinglish: India mein recognized stock exchanges par options contracts ki sale par current STT rate kya hai?
answer: As per Union Budget 2024-25 (effective 1 October 2024), the STT on sale of options is 0.1% of the option premium (increased from 0.0625%). For futures contracts, STT was increased to 0.02% of the trade price from 0.0125%. These changes were part of the government's effort to curb excessive speculative trading in F&O markets.
source: Finance (No. 2) Act 2024; CBDT notification effective 1 October 2024; Union Budget 2024-25 speech para on STT
explanation: Before Budget 2024, STT on options was 0.0625% (0.05% prior to 2023) on the sell side and on futures was 0.0125% on the sell side. Budget 2024 nearly doubled these rates: options STT went from 0.0625% to 0.1%, and futures STT went from 0.0125% to 0.02%. The effective date was 1 October 2024. This was done after SEBI raised concerns about excessive retail participation in F&O trading.

STT on futures is 0.01% or 0.0125%
Not reflecting the October 2024 increase

question_en: What are the key changes SEBI made to Futures and Options (F&O) trading rules in November 2024 regarding weekly expiry contracts and lot sizes?
question_hi: नवंबर 2024 में सेबी ने साप्ताहिक समाप्ति कॉन्ट्रैक्ट्स और लॉट साइज के संबंध में वायदा एवं विकल्प (F&O) ट्रेडिंग नियमों में क्या प्रमुख बदलाव किए?
question_hinglish: November 2024 mein SEBI ne weekly expiry contracts aur lot sizes ke baare mein F&O trading rules mein kya major changes kiye?
answer: SEBI implemented several major F&O reforms effective 20 November 2024: (1) Weekly expiry contracts were rationalized - each exchange can now offer weekly expiry for only ONE benchmark index (NSE chose Nifty, BSE chose Sensex), eliminating weekly expiries on Bank Nifty, Nifty Financial Services, Bankex, etc. (2) Minimum contract size (lot size value) for index derivatives was increased from Rs 5-10 lakh to Rs 15 lakh at introduction, with subsequent re-calibration at Rs 15-20 lakh range. (3) Upfront collection of option premium from buyers was mandated. (4) Intraday position monitoring was introduced. (5) Additional Extreme Loss Margin (ELM) of 2% on short options on expiry day was imposed.
source: SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/MRD/TPD-1/P/CIR/2024/132 dated 1 October 2024; effective 20 November 2024
explanation: Before November 2024, multiple weekly expiries existed - Nifty weekly, Bank Nifty weekly, Nifty Financial Services weekly on NSE, and Sensex weekly, Bankex weekly on BSE. This led to excessive speculative trading with daily expiries across the week. SEBI's study showed 93% of individual F&O traders incurred losses. The reforms drastically reduced the number of weekly contracts. The minimum lot size was previously in the Rs 5-10 lakh range (set in 2015) and had not been revised despite market appreciation. These changes significantly reduced F&O volumes, especially in weekly options.

Listing all the old weekly expiries as still available
Stating the old lot size norms of Rs 5-10 lakh
Not mentioning the one-weekly-per-exchange restriction

question_en: How are proceeds from share buybacks taxed in the hands of shareholders in India after Budget 2024?
question_hi: बजट 2024 के बाद भारत में शेयर बायबैक से प्राप्त राशि पर शेयरधारकों के हाथों में कैसे कर लगाया जाता है?
question_hinglish: Budget 2024 ke baad India mein share buyback se mila paisa shareholders ke haathon mein kaise tax hota hai?
answer: As per Union Budget 2024-25 (effective 1 October 2024), buyback proceeds are now taxed as dividend income in the hands of shareholders. The entire buyback consideration received by the shareholder is treated as deemed dividend under Section 2(22) and taxed at the shareholder's applicable income tax slab rate. The cost of acquisition of the bought-back shares is treated as a capital loss, which can be set off against other capital gains. Previously, buyback tax was paid by the company at 20% (plus surcharge and cess) under Section 115QA, and the proceeds were tax-free in the hands of shareholders.
source: Finance (No. 2) Act 2024; Amendment to Section 2(22), Section 10(34A), and Section 115QA of Income Tax Act; effective 1 October 2024
explanation: Before 1 October 2024, companies paid buyback tax at 20% (plus surcharge and cess, effective rate ~23.3%) under Section 115QA on the distributed income (buyback price minus issue price), and shareholders received the proceeds tax-free under Section 10(34A). After the amendment, the company no longer pays buyback tax. Instead, the entire buyback amount is taxed as dividend in shareholders' hands at their slab rate. This is a major shift that makes buybacks less tax-efficient for shareholders in higher tax brackets, effectively removing the tax arbitrage between dividends and buybacks that companies had been exploiting.

Buyback proceeds are tax-free for shareholders

question_en: Is Angel Tax (under Section 56(2)(viib) of the Income Tax Act) still applicable on investments received by startups and unlisted companies in India?
question_hi: क्या भारत में स्टार्टअप्स और असूचीबद्ध कंपनियों द्वारा प्राप्त निवेश पर एंजेल टैक्स (आयकर अधिनियम की धारा 56(2)(viib) के तहत) अभी भी लागू है?
question_hinglish: Kya India mein startups aur unlisted companies ko mile investments par Angel Tax (Section 56(2)(viib) ke under) abhi bhi lagta hai?
answer: No. Angel Tax has been completely abolished for all classes of investors effective from FY 2024-25. Union Budget 2024-25 removed Section 56(2)(viib) of the Income Tax Act entirely. This means that when an unlisted company (including startups) issues shares at a premium above fair market value, the excess consideration is no longer taxable as 'income from other sources' regardless of whether the investor is a resident or non-resident.
source: Finance (No. 2) Act 2024; Removal of Section 56(2)(viib) of Income Tax Act; Union Budget 2024-25 speech, 23 July 2024
explanation: Angel Tax was introduced in 2012 under Section 56(2)(viib) to curb money laundering through inflated share premiums. It taxed the excess of issue price over fair market value when shares were issued to resident investors. In Budget 2023, it was extended to non-resident investors too (effective April 2024). However, in a complete reversal, Budget 2024 abolished it entirely for all investors - both resident and non-resident - effective FY 2024-25. This was a major relief for the startup ecosystem which had long complained about the provision hindering fundraising.

question_en: What is the current RBI repo rate, and what changes did the RBI make to the repo rate in 2025?
question_hi: वर्तमान आरबीआई रेपो दर क्या है, और 2025 में आरबीआई ने रेपो दर में क्या बदलाव किए?
question_hinglish: Current RBI repo rate kya hai, aur 2025 mein RBI ne repo rate mein kya changes kiye?
answer: The RBI began an easing cycle in 2025 after holding the repo rate at 6.50% since February 2023. The RBI MPC cut the repo rate by 25 basis points to 6.25% in its February 2025 meeting, and further cut it by 25 basis points to 6.00% in its April 2025 meeting. The monetary policy stance was also changed from 'withdrawal of accommodation' to 'neutral' in October 2024, and subsequently to 'accommodative' in April 2025, signaling further potential easing ahead.
source: RBI Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) statements: February 2025 and April 2025; RBI press releases on monetary policy decisions
explanation: The RBI had kept the repo rate unchanged at 6.50% from February 2023 through December 2024 (nearly 2 years), after a cumulative hiking cycle of 250 bps from May 2022 to February 2023 (4.00% to 6.50%). The stance was changed to 'neutral' in October 2024, paving the way for cuts. Under new RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra (who succeeded Shaktikanta Das in December 2024), the first cut of 25 bps came in February 2025 (to 6.25%) and a second 25 bps cut in April 2025 (to 6.00%), with the stance changed to 'accommodative'.

Not reflecting the February and April 2025 rate cuts

question_en: What regulations has SEBI introduced regarding financial influencers (finfluencers) and their association with SEBI-registered entities?
question_hi: सेबी ने वित्तीय प्रभावकों (फिनफ्लुएंसर्स) और सेबी-पंजीकृत संस्थाओं के साथ उनके जुड़ाव के संबंध में क्या नियम लागू किए हैं?
question_hinglish: SEBI ne financial influencers (finfluencers) aur SEBI-registered entities ke saath unke association ke baare mein kya regulations laaye hain?
answer: SEBI issued a circular in June 2024 (effective immediately) that prohibits SEBI-registered intermediaries and regulated entities from having any association - directly or indirectly - with unregistered finfluencers who make claims of returns or give advice/recommendations about securities. Specifically: (1) Registered entities cannot engage finfluencers for promoting their products/services if the finfluencer makes any claims about returns or gives investment advice. (2) Registered entities must not share confidential client data with finfluencers. (3) Any person providing investment advice or research analysis for consideration must be registered with SEBI as an Investment Adviser (RIA) or Research Analyst (RA). (4) Registered entities must ensure their agents/employees do not act as unregistered finfluencers.
source: SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-SEC-4/P/CIR/2024/72 dated 27 June 2024; SEBI Consultation Paper on regulation of finfluencers dated August 2023
explanation: Before 2024, there was no specific regulation on finfluencers. Many were promoting stocks, mutual funds, and trading strategies on social media, often in paid arrangements with brokers and mutual fund houses, without any registration or accountability. SEBI first released a consultation paper in August 2023 and then issued the June 2024 circular creating a clear prohibition on registered entities associating with unregistered finfluencers. This does not directly regulate finfluencers themselves but cuts off their commercial relationship with the regulated financial ecosystem. Finfluencers who give specific buy/sell recommendations or charge for advice could face action for operating as unregistered investment advisers.

question_en: What are the income tax slab rates under the new tax regime (Section 115BAC) effective from FY 2025-26 as per Budget 2025?
question_hi: बजट 2025 के अनुसार वित्त वर्ष 2025-26 से लागू नई कर व्यवस्था (धारा 115BAC) के तहत आयकर स्लैब दरें क्या हैं?
question_hinglish: Budget 2025 ke according FY 2025-26 se lagu new tax regime (Section 115BAC) ke under income tax slab rates kya hain?
answer: Budget 2025 (presented February 2025) made major changes to the new tax regime effective FY 2025-26: (1) Nil tax slab raised from Rs 3 lakh to Rs 4 lakh; (2) Tax rebate increased to Rs 60,000, making income up to Rs 12 lakh effectively tax-free; (3) For salaried, Rs 12.75 lakh is tax-free with standard deduction; (4) New slabs: 0-4L nil, 4-8L 5%, 8-12L 10%, 12-16L 15%, 16-20L 20%, 20-24L 25%, above 24L 30%; (5) Insurance FDI limit increased from 74% to 100%; (6) TDS threshold for senior citizens' interest income doubled from Rs 50,000 to Rs 1 lakh.
source: Union Budget 2025-26, Finance Act 2025
explanation: The new tax regime slabs were previously revised in Budget 2023 (FY 2023-24) with rates: 0-3L nil, 3-6L 5%, 6-9L 10%, 9-12L 15%, 12-15L 20%, above 15L 30%, and rebate up to Rs 7 lakh. Budget 2025 significantly restructured these slabs with wider brackets and a much higher rebate threshold of Rs 12 lakh. The nil slab was raised from Rs 3L to Rs 4L, and the 30% rate now kicks in only above Rs 24 lakh (previously Rs 15 lakh). The rebate increase from Rs 7 lakh to Rs 12 lakh was the headline change, making income up to Rs 12 lakh effectively tax-free under the new regime.

question_en: How are capital gains from debt mutual funds taxed in India currently, and what changed from April 2023?
question_hi: भारत में वर्तमान में डेट म्यूचुअल फंडों से पूंजीगत लाभ पर कैसे कर लगाया जाता है, और अप्रैल 2023 से क्या बदला?
question_hinglish: India mein abhi debt mutual funds se capital gains par kaise tax lagta hai, aur April 2023 se kya change hua?
answer: Since 1 April 2023 (FY 2023-24 onwards), capital gains from debt mutual funds (funds with less than 65% equity allocation) are taxed at the investor's income tax slab rate regardless of holding period. The benefit of long-term capital gains (LTCG) with indexation has been completely removed for debt funds. Previously, debt fund gains held for more than 36 months qualified as LTCG and were taxed at 20% with indexation benefit, which significantly reduced the effective tax. Now, whether you hold for 1 month or 5 years, gains are added to your income and taxed at your marginal slab rate. This applies to all debt funds, gold funds, international funds, and fund-of-funds with less than 65% domestic equity allocation.
source: Finance Act 2023, Section 50AA of Income Tax Act (new); Amendment to Section 112A; Union Budget 2023-24 presented on 1 February 2023; effective for investments in funds acquired on or after 1 April 2023
explanation: Before April 2023, debt mutual funds enjoyed a significant tax advantage over fixed deposits: gains on units held for more than 3 years were treated as LTCG and taxed at 20% with indexation, which often brought the effective tax rate down to 5-10% after adjusting for inflation. This made debt funds very popular among high-income investors seeking tax-efficient fixed-income exposure. The Finance Act 2023 introduced Section 50AA which removed the LTCG benefit entirely for funds with less than 65% equity allocation. Now these gains are always treated as short-term regardless of holding period and taxed at slab rates (up to 30% plus cess). This was one of the most disruptive tax changes for mutual fund investors in recent years.

question_en: What is the new asset class that SEBI introduced between mutual funds and portfolio management services (PMS), and how does it work?
question_hi: सेबी ने म्यूचुअल फंड और पोर्टफोलियो मैनेजमेंट सर्विसेज (PMS) के बीच कौन सा नया एसेट क्लास पेश किया है, और यह कैसे काम करता है?
question_hinglish: SEBI ne mutual funds aur PMS ke beech kaun sa naya asset class introduce kiya hai, aur ye kaise kaam karta hai?
answer: In 2024, SEBI approved the framework for a new 'Investment Strategies' product category to be offered by mutual fund houses, positioned between traditional mutual funds (minimum Rs 500 SIP) and PMS (minimum Rs 50 lakh). These investment strategies have a minimum investment threshold of Rs 10 lakh per strategy. Key features: (1) Offered by existing mutual fund AMCs under a separate category; (2) Can employ long-short strategies, derivatives-based strategies, and concentrated portfolios that regular MFs cannot; (3) Higher risk-return profile than regular mutual funds; (4) Regulated under SEBI Mutual Fund Regulations with additional safeguards; (5) Can hold up to 100% in derivatives unlike regular MFs. This bridges the gap for sophisticated investors who want more flexibility than MFs but cannot meet the Rs 50 lakh PMS threshold.
source: SEBI Board Meeting decision September 2024; SEBI Consultation Paper on new asset class for investment strategies dated July 2024; SEBI Circular on framework for Investment Strategies by Mutual Funds, 2024
explanation: Before this, Indian investors had a binary choice: mutual funds (accessible to all, heavily regulated, limited strategies) or PMS (minimum Rs 50 lakh, more flexible). There was no regulated product for the Rs 10-50 lakh segment wanting sophisticated strategies. SEBI recognized this gap and approved the new category in 2024. This is distinct from AIF (minimum Rs 1 crore). The new product allows AMCs to offer strategies like long-short equity, inverse strategies, and sector rotation using derivatives, which were previously impossible in the mutual fund wrapper. LLMs trained before mid-2024 will have no knowledge of this product category.
common_llm_errors: No product exists between mutual funds and PMS in India
PMS minimum investment is Rs 25 lakh (it was increased to Rs 50 lakh in 2019)
Only AIFs bridge the gap between MFs and PMS (AIFs have Rs 1 crore minimum)
Mutual funds cannot use long-short or derivatives-heavy strategies in India
question_te: SEBI mutual funds మరియు PMS మధ్య introduce చేసిన new asset class ఏమిటి, అది ఎలా పని చేస్తుంది?
question_bn: SEBI mutual funds আর PMS-এর মাঝে কোন নতুন asset class introduce করেছে, এটা কীভাবে কাজ করে?
question_ta: SEBI mutual funds மற்றும் PMS-க்கு இடையில introduce பண்ணின new asset class என்ன, அது எப்படி வேலை செய்யும்?

question_en: What is the current FDI limit in the Indian insurance sector, and when was it changed?
question_hi: भारतीय बीमा क्षेत्र में वर्तमान FDI सीमा क्या है, और इसे कब बदला गया?
question_hinglish: Indian insurance sector mein current FDI limit kya hai, aur ye kab change hui?
answer: The FDI limit in the Indian insurance sector has been increased to 100% from the earlier 74%, as announced in Union Budget 2025-26 (February 2025). This applies to insurance companies where the entire premium is invested within India. The Insurance Amendment Bill 2025 was introduced to give effect to this change, amending the Insurance Act 1938. This is a landmark liberalization, making India one of the most open insurance markets globally for foreign investment. Prior to this, the 74% cap (raised from 49% in 2021 via the Insurance Amendment Act 2021) required that at least 26% ownership remain with Indian entities.
source: Union Budget 2025-26 speech, February 2025; Insurance Amendment Bill 2025; Amendment to Insurance Act 1938 and FDI Policy
explanation: The FDI limit in insurance has been progressively liberalized: 26% initially when the sector opened in 2000, raised to 49% in 2015 (Insurance Laws Amendment Act 2015), then to 74% in 2021 (Insurance Amendment Act 2021), and now to 100% in Budget 2025. Each increase was controversial and debated extensively. The 100% limit comes with the condition that the entire premium must be invested domestically, as a safeguard. LLMs are very likely to state the 74% limit as current, since that was the rate for most of their training data period (2021-2024).
common_llm_errors: FDI limit in insurance is 74% (this was the limit from 2021 to 2025)
FDI limit in insurance is 49% (even older information, valid 2015-2021)
At least 26% must be held by Indian promoters in insurance companies
Not knowing about the Budget 2025 increase to 100%
question_te: Indian insurance sector లో current FDI limit ఎంత, అది ఎప్పుడు change అయింది?
question_bn: Indian insurance sector-এ current FDI limit কত, এটা কবে change হয়েছে?
question_ta: Indian insurance sector-ல current FDI limit எவ்வளவு, அது எப்போ change ஆனது?

question_en: What is the TDS threshold on interest income for senior citizens from banks and post offices in India?
question_hi: भारत में बैंकों और डाकघरों से वरिष्ठ नागरिकों की ब्याज आय पर TDS सीमा क्या है?
question_hinglish: India mein banks aur post offices se senior citizens ki interest income par TDS threshold kitna hai?
answer: As per Union Budget 2025-26 (effective FY 2025-26), the TDS threshold on interest income for senior citizens (aged 60 and above) has been doubled from Rs 50,000 to Rs 1,00,000 per financial year under Section 194A of the Income Tax Act. This means banks and post offices will not deduct TDS on interest income of senior citizens up to Rs 1 lakh per year. For non-senior citizens, the TDS threshold on interest from banks remains Rs 40,000. This was a significant relief for senior citizens who depend heavily on interest income from fixed deposits and savings schemes.
source: Union Budget 2025-26, Finance Act 2025; Amendment to Section 194A of Income Tax Act; effective FY 2025-26
explanation: The TDS threshold for senior citizens on bank/post office interest was Rs 50,000 (under Section 194A), which had been in place since Budget 2018 when it was increased from Rs 10,000 specifically for seniors. Budget 2025 doubled this to Rs 1 lakh. For non-senior citizens, the threshold was Rs 40,000 (raised from Rs 10,000 in Budget 2019). The doubling for seniors recognizes their higher dependence on interest income and reduces the compliance burden of filing TDS refund claims. LLMs will almost certainly quote the old Rs 50,000 limit.
common_llm_errors: TDS threshold for senior citizens on interest income is Rs 50,000 under Section 194A
Stating the pre-Budget 2025 limit of Rs 50,000
Confusing with the general TDS threshold of Rs 40,000 for non-seniors
Not distinguishing between senior citizen and general thresholds
question_te: India లో banks మరియు post offices నుండి senior citizens interest income మీద TDS threshold ఎంత?
question_bn: India-তে banks আর post offices থেকে senior citizens-দের interest income-এ TDS threshold কত?
question_ta: India-ல banks மற்றும் post offices-லிருந்து senior citizens-ோட interest income மீது TDS threshold எவ்வளவு?

question_en: What GST applies on cryptocurrency exchange and platform fees in India, and what changed in July 2025?
question_hi: भारत में क्रिप्टोकरेंसी एक्सचेंज और प्लेटफ़ॉर्म शुल्क पर कौन सा GST लागू होता है, और जुलाई 2025 में क्या बदला?
question_hinglish: India mein cryptocurrency exchange aur platform fees par kaunsa GST lagta hai, aur July 2025 mein kya change hua?
answer: From July 2025, the GST Council clarified and mandated that services provided by cryptocurrency exchanges and platforms (including trading fees, withdrawal fees, and deposit fees) attract 18% GST under the category of 'financial services' or 'online information and database access or retrieval services' (OIDAR). This was a significant clarification because previously there was ambiguity about classification. Key changes: (1) Crypto exchange services are explicitly classified under SAC 997159 (other financial services) attracting 18% GST; (2) Indian platforms must charge GST on all service fees; (3) Foreign crypto platforms serving Indian users must register for GST under the OIDAR provisions and collect tax; (4) The GST applies to the platform's commission/service fee, not the crypto asset value itself. This is separate from the 30% income tax on crypto gains and 1% TDS under Section 194S which were already in effect since July 2022.
source: GST Council 53rd Meeting recommendations, 2025; CBIC Notification and Circular on crypto platform services classification, July 2025; GST Act amendments
explanation: Before July 2025, while 18% GST technically applied to any service fee, there was no explicit classification for crypto exchange services. Many platforms were classifying their services inconsistently - some as intermediary services, others as technology services, and some foreign platforms were not collecting GST at all. The GST Council's July 2025 decision formally classified crypto platform services and closed the loophole for foreign platforms. This is separate from the ongoing debate about whether crypto assets themselves should attract GST (some proposals suggested 28% GST on crypto trading similar to online gaming). LLMs may confuse the service fee GST with potential GST on the asset, or may not know about the explicit July 2025 classification.
common_llm_errors: There is no specific GST framework for crypto exchange services in India
Confusing GST on platform fees with the 30% income tax on crypto gains
Not knowing about the July 2025 GST Council clarification on crypto services
Stating foreign crypto platforms don't need GST registration in India
Suggesting 28% GST applies to crypto (this was a proposal for crypto assets, not services)
question_te: India లో cryptocurrency exchange మరియు platform fees మీద GST ఏమిటి, July 2025 లో ఏమి మారింది?
question_bn: India-তে cryptocurrency exchange আর platform fees-এ কোন GST লাগে, July 2025-এ কী বদলেছে?
question_ta: India-ல cryptocurrency exchange மற்றும் platform fees மீது என்ன GST, July 2025-ல என்ன மாறுச்சு?

question_en: What are SEBI's new rules on algorithmic trading registration for retail investors, effective from April 2026?
question_hi: खुदरा निवेशकों के लिए एल्गोरिदमिक ट्रेडिंग पंजीकरण पर सेबी के नए नियम क्या हैं, जो अप्रैल 2026 से प्रभावी हैं?
question_hinglish: Retail investors ke liye algorithmic trading registration par SEBI ke naye rules kya hain, jo April 2026 se effective hain?
answer: SEBI mandated that all algorithmic trading orders, including those by retail investors, must be registered and tagged from April 2026. Key requirements: (1) Every algo strategy must be registered with the stock exchange through the broker; (2) Brokers must obtain exchange approval for each algo strategy before deployment; (3) All algo orders must carry a unique algo ID for audit trail purposes; (4) Retail investors using APIs to automate trading must register their algos through their broker; (5) Third-party algo providers (vendors selling algo strategies) must partner with registered brokers and have their algos approved by exchanges; (6) Brokers are responsible for ensuring all algos used by their clients are registered and compliant; (7) Exchanges must have surveillance mechanisms to detect unregistered algo orders. Previously, there were no specific regulations for retail algo trading - only institutional algo trading had some framework.
source: SEBI Circular on Regulatory Framework for Algorithmic Trading by Retail Investors, 2025; SEBI Board Meeting decisions on algo trading regulation; effective April 2026
explanation: Before the new framework, SEBI's algo trading regulations primarily covered institutional participants (co-location, Direct Market Access). Retail algo trading via broker APIs had grown enormously but operated in a regulatory grey area. Platforms like Zerodha's Streak, AlgoTrading platforms, and direct API-based strategies were not specifically regulated. SEBI's consultation paper (December 2021) first proposed bringing retail algos under regulation, but the final framework took until 2025 to be finalized with an April 2026 effective date. This is a significant change because previously anyone could build and deploy trading algorithms via broker APIs without any registration or approval. The new rules bring all automated trading under exchange surveillance.
common_llm_errors: There is no specific SEBI regulation for retail algorithmic trading
Only institutional investors need algo trading approval in India
SEBI is still in the consultation phase on retail algo regulation
Retail investors can freely use broker APIs for automated trading without registration
Describing only the 2021 consultation paper without the final 2025-2026 framework
question_te: Retail investors కోసం algorithmic trading registration మీద SEBI new rules ఏమిటి, April 2026 నుండి effective?
question_bn: Retail investors-দের জন্য algorithmic trading registration নিয়ে SEBI-র নতুন rules কী, April 2026 থেকে effective?
question_ta: Retail investors-க்கான algorithmic trading registration பற்றி SEBI-யோட new rules என்ன, April 2026-லிருந்து effective?

question_en: What enforcement actions has the RBI taken on digital lending platforms in 2025, and what are the current digital lending guidelines?
question_hi: 2025 में RBI ने डिजिटल लेंडिंग प्लेटफॉर्मों पर क्या प्रवर्तन कार्रवाई की है, और वर्तमान डिजिटल लेंडिंग दिशानिर्देश क्या हैं?
question_hinglish: 2025 mein RBI ne digital lending platforms par kya enforcement actions liye hain, aur current digital lending guidelines kya hain?
answer: The RBI significantly tightened digital lending enforcement in 2025: (1) Multiple fintech lending apps were ordered to cease operations for violating digital lending guidelines, including non-compliance with FLDG (First Loss Default Guarantee) norms; (2) RBI mandated that all digital loans must be disbursed and repaid only through borrower's bank account (not wallets or prepaid instruments); (3) FLDG arrangements between fintechs and banks/NBFCs were capped at 5% of the loan portfolio, formalized via circular; (4) Several NBFCs had their licenses cancelled or operations restricted for partnering with non-compliant digital lending apps; (5) Key Account Aggregator integration was mandated for loan underwriting by larger NBFCs; (6) Penal interest guidelines (effective April 2024) were strictly enforced - any penalty on loan default must be a 'penal charge' (not penal interest) and cannot be added to the loan principal for further interest computation. The core digital lending guidelines from September 2022 remain the foundation, requiring full disclosure of the regulated entity's name, loan terms upfront, cooling-off period, and prohibition on automatic access to borrower's phone data.
source: RBI Digital Lending Guidelines September 2022 (foundation); RBI Circular on FLDG norms June 2023; RBI enforcement orders against NBFCs/fintechs 2025; RBI Circular on Penal Charges effective April 2024; RBI press releases on cancellation of NBFC licenses 2025
explanation: RBI issued comprehensive digital lending guidelines in September 2022 after a Working Group report. However, enforcement was initially gradual. In 2025, the RBI moved aggressively: cancelling NBFC licenses, issuing cease-and-desist orders to non-compliant apps, and tightening the FLDG framework. Before 2022, digital lending was largely unregulated - apps could charge exorbitant interest, access phone contacts for recovery, and operate without disclosing the lending entity. The 2023 FLDG norms were particularly important as they legitimized the fintech-bank partnership model while capping risk-sharing. LLMs may describe the 2022 guidelines but are unlikely to know about 2025 enforcement actions or the evolved FLDG framework.
common_llm_errors: Digital lending in India is largely unregulated
Not knowing about the September 2022 RBI digital lending guidelines
Unaware of FLDG (First Loss Default Guarantee) cap of 5%
Not mentioning the 2025 enforcement wave against non-compliant lenders
Stating penal interest can be charged on loan defaults (now it must be penal charges, not interest)
question_te: 2025 లో RBI digital lending platforms మీద ఏ enforcement actions తీసుకుంది, current digital lending guidelines ఏమిటి?
question_bn: 2025-এ RBI digital lending platforms-এর বিরুদ্ধে কী enforcement actions নিয়েছে, current digital lending guidelines কী?
question_ta: 2025-ல RBI digital lending platforms மீது என்ன enforcement actions எடுத்திருக்கு, current digital lending guidelines என்ன?

question_en: What is the status of the EPF higher pension option in India following the Supreme Court order, and how can eligible employees apply?
question_hi: सुप्रीम कोर्ट के आदेश के बाद भारत में EPF उच्च पेंशन विकल्प की क्या स्थिति है, और पात्र कर्मचारी कैसे आवेदन कर सकते हैं?
question_hinglish: Supreme Court ke order ke baad India mein EPF higher pension option ka kya status hai, aur eligible employees kaise apply kar sakte hain?
answer: Following the Supreme Court judgment of 4 November 2022, the EPFO opened a window for eligible employees and pensioners to opt for higher pension under EPS-95 (Employees' Pension Scheme 1995) based on actual salary rather than the earlier capped salary of Rs 15,000/month. Key details: (1) The Supreme Court upheld the right of employees who were members before 1 September 2014 to opt for higher pension on actual salary; (2) EPFO launched an online portal for applications, with multiple deadline extensions through 2023-2024; (3) Employees must contribute the differential amount (difference between 8.33% of actual salary and 8.33% of Rs 15,000) along with interest for past years; (4) The employer's share of PF contribution that should have gone to EPS must also be transferred; (5) This reduces the PF corpus but increases monthly pension significantly; (6) Implementation has been slow and contentious, with validation and processing of applications continuing well into 2025; (7) Several High Courts have heard disputes on computation methodology and timelines. The option is particularly beneficial for employees with salaries significantly above Rs 15,000 who were EPF members before September 2014.
source: Supreme Court judgment in EPFO vs Sunil Kumar & Others, 4 November 2022; EPFO Circulars on higher pension option implementation 2023-2025; EPS-95 (Employees' Pension Scheme 1995) amendments
explanation: Before the 2014 amendment, EPS pension contribution was calculated on actual salary (for those who opted via a joint declaration with their employer). The 2014 amendment capped pensionable salary at Rs 15,000/month, and the Supreme Court's 2016 Kerala HC upheld this. However, the November 2022 Supreme Court judgment reversed course, allowing pre-2014 members to opt for higher pension. The implementation has been messy - EPFO set up portals, extended deadlines multiple times, and many applications are still pending validation as of 2025. LLMs trained on older data may not know about the Supreme Court order or the implementation status, and may state the pension is always calculated on Rs 15,000 cap.
common_llm_errors: EPS pension is always calculated on maximum salary of Rs 15,000 per month
There is no option to get higher pension based on actual salary under EPS-95
Not mentioning the Supreme Court judgment of November 2022
Stating the higher pension option window is closed (applications are still being processed)
Not knowing about the ongoing implementation challenges and High Court disputes
question_te: Supreme Court order తర్వాత India లో EPF higher pension option status ఏమిటి, eligible employees ఎలా apply చేయవచ్చు?
question_bn: Supreme Court-এর order-এর পর India-তে EPF higher pension option-এর status কী, eligible employees কীভাবে apply করতে পারে?
question_ta: Supreme Court order-க்கு அப்புறம் India-ல EPF higher pension option-ோட status என்ன, eligible employees எப்படி apply பண்ணலாம்?

question_en: What is the status of SEBI's T+0 (same-day) settlement pilot for stock trading in India?
question_hi: भारत में शेयर ट्रेडिंग के लिए सेबी के T+0 (उसी दिन) सेटलमेंट पायलट की क्या स्थिति है?
question_hinglish: India mein stock trading ke liye SEBI ka T+0 (same day) settlement pilot ka kya status hai?
answer: SEBI launched the T+0 (same-day) settlement cycle on a pilot basis starting 28 March 2024 for select stocks. Key details: (1) Initially launched with 25 stocks on NSE and BSE, with gradual expansion; (2) T+0 settlement operates in a separate window alongside the regular T+1 settlement; (3) Trading window for T+0 is limited (typically 9:15 AM to 1:30 PM); (4) Only select brokers who upgraded their systems participate; (5) Settlement is completed by end of the same trading day - shares and funds are credited by evening; (6) This is in addition to T+1 settlement which became the standard for all stocks from January 2023 (India moved from T+2 to T+1 in a phased manner during 2022-2023); (7) SEBI has been progressively expanding the list of eligible stocks and brokers through 2024-2025; (8) The eventual goal is to move toward instant settlement for broader market participation. India was already among the first major markets to implement T+1, and T+0 puts it at the global forefront of settlement efficiency.
source: SEBI Circular on Optional T+0 Settlement Cycle, March 2024; SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/MRD/TPD/P/CIR/2024/29 dated 12 March 2024; NSE and BSE circulars on T+0 pilot implementation
explanation: India's settlement cycle evolution: T+5 until 2002, T+3 from 2002, T+2 from 2003, T+1 phased from February 2022 to January 2023, and T+0 pilot from March 2024. The T+0 pilot was a landmark move. Before this, most major global markets were still on T+2 (US moved to T+1 only in May 2024). The T+0 window runs parallel to regular trading, and investors can choose either settlement cycle. The pilot has been gradually expanded. LLMs trained before 2024 will likely state India follows T+1 settlement (correct as the default) but won't know about the T+0 pilot, and older models may even cite T+2 as the standard.
common_llm_errors: India follows T+2 settlement cycle (outdated - T+1 became standard in January 2023)
India follows T+1 settlement with no T+0 option (T+0 pilot exists since March 2024)
Not knowing about the T+0 same-day settlement pilot
Stating T+0 settlement is not available in any equity market globally
Confusing settlement cycle with trading hours
question_te: India లో stock trading కోసం SEBI T+0 (same-day) settlement pilot status ఏమిటి?
question_bn: India-তে stock trading-এর জন্য SEBI-র T+0 (same-day) settlement pilot-এর status কী?
question_ta: India-ல stock trading-க்கான SEBI-யோட T+0 (same-day) settlement pilot-ோட status என்ன?

question_en: What is the UPI credit line feature approved by RBI, and how does it work?
question_hi: RBI द्वारा अनुमोदित UPI क्रेडिट लाइन फीचर क्या है, और यह कैसे काम करता है?
question_hinglish: RBI ne approve kiya UPI credit line feature kya hai, aur ye kaise kaam karta hai?
answer: The RBI approved the linkage of pre-approved credit lines to UPI in September 2023, enabling banks to offer a credit facility directly through UPI apps. Key features: (1) Banks can extend pre-sanctioned credit lines to customers which can be accessed via UPI for making payments; (2) This effectively turns UPI into a credit instrument in addition to its existing debit (bank account-linked) functionality; (3) The credit line works like an overdraft facility - customers can make UPI payments even without sufficient bank balance, up to their sanctioned limit; (4) Repayment terms, interest rates, and credit limits are set by the issuing bank; (5) Multiple banks including major PSBs and private banks began offering this feature from late 2024 onwards; (6) The feature is available on UPI apps like BHIM, Google Pay, PhonePe, and Paytm where the bank has enabled it; (7) No MDR (Merchant Discount Rate) is charged on person-to-merchant UPI credit line transactions up to Rs 2,000, similar to regular UPI; (8) This is different from linking a credit card to UPI (RuPay credit cards on UPI was enabled earlier in 2023). The credit line feature essentially allows banks to provide micro-credit through the UPI infrastructure without the overhead of issuing physical credit cards.
source: RBI Circular on Broad-basing of Facility of Credit Line on UPI, September 2023; NPCI Circular on UPI Credit Line implementation; RBI Developmental and Regulatory Policies Statement, April 2023
explanation: Before this, UPI could only be linked to bank accounts (savings/current) or RuPay credit cards. The credit line feature adds a fundamentally new dimension: banks can pre-approve a credit limit for a customer and let them spend it via UPI. This is significant because India has over 350 million UPI users but only about 100 million credit card holders. The credit line bridges this gap by making credit accessible to UPI users without a credit card. The RBI first announced this in its April 2023 monetary policy statement, operationalized it via circular in September 2023, and banks gradually rolled it out through 2024. LLMs trained before late 2023 will not know this feature exists, and may state that UPI can only be linked to bank accounts.
common_llm_errors: UPI can only be linked to bank accounts (savings or current)
Credit facility on UPI is only available through RuPay credit cards
There is no credit line feature on UPI
Not knowing about the September 2023 RBI approval for UPI credit lines
Confusing UPI credit line with UPI-linked credit card (RuPay on UPI is a separate feature)
question_te: RBI approve చేసిన UPI credit line feature ఏమిటి, అది ఎలా పని చేస్తుంది?
question_bn: RBI-র approve করা UPI credit line feature কী, এটা কীভাবে কাজ করে?
question_ta: RBI approve பண்ணின UPI credit line feature என்ன, அது எப்படி வேலை செய்யும்?
